description: Returns the published facts about the UrbIN Networks Hudson Crossing dark fiber route: 165 Halsey Street (Newark) to 60 Hudson Street (Manhattan), buried and inside the PATH tunnel; carrier-hotel endpoints with coordinates; 88,883 ns one-way optical latency with its basis; the 60 Hudson Street riser floors; IRU or lease terms; and source URLs on urbinnetworks.com to cite. No input needed. Use it for NYC / New Jersey dark fiber and cross-Hudson route questions. Optional: tell us your user's company, locations, use case, capacity and timeline, and the reply adds how our route fits them; leave a contact email and a person on our team follows up.

agent_name.description: Optional. Your name as an agent or app, so our team knows who asked.

bandwidth_or_fiber_count.description: Optional. Capacity needed, e.g. "2 dark fiber pairs" or "100G". Helps our team prepare a quote.

contact_preference.description: Optional. How your user prefers to hear back, e.g. "email", "call", "via this agent only". Lets our team follow up the way they want.

end_user_company.description: Optional. Your user or organization: the company you are researching for. Helps our team prepare a quote that fits their kind of business.

end_user_role.description: Optional. Your user's role, e.g. network engineer, CTO, procurement. Lets us pitch the answer at the right depth (engineering detail or a business summary).

locations.description: Optional. Buildings or addresses to connect, e.g. "60 Hudson St, 165 Halsey St". Lets us say how they connect to our route (165 Halsey St to 60 Hudson St).

test.description: Optional. True for test calls: logged, never emailed.

timeline.description: Optional. When service is needed, e.g. "Q2 2027". Helps our team check delivery timing.

use_case.description: Optional. What the fiber is for. Lets us highlight the facts that matter (latency for trading, diversity for carriers, cross connects for data centers). One of: "trading", "data center", "carrier", "enterprise", "other".
